calls.body: The Mammoth are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Oilers are near the top at keeping shots away. We’ll side with the Mammoth.

calls.head: The Oilers don’t own Vejmelka
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Vejmelka has been shaky against the Oilers, well below his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if he’s back to his usual self.
calls.call: If Vejmelka starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .899 than to his .849 against the Oilers.

calls.head: The Mammoth roll four lines, the Oilers lean on their top six
calls.body: On depth, Utah is the league’s best, but Edmonton is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Mammoth.

surprises.head: Edmonton couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Utah usually allows more dangerous shots than most teams. Not tonight: Edmonton’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 4.2% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.5% (about 6.7% against Utah) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 80 games.

story.head: The Mammoth take down the Oilers
paras: Barrett Hayton got the scoring started for the Mammoth on the power play midway through the first. Clayton Keller stretched the lead to 2-0 on the power play midway through the second. Leon Draisaitl got the Oilers on the board 1:57 later. Logan Cooley stretched the lead to 3-1, 23 seconds later, the eventual winner. Shakir Mukhamadullin scored his first goal for Edmonton on the power play early in the third to pull the Oilers within one with the goalie pulled. Keller struck again with 28 seconds left into the empty net with 28 seconds left.

The Mammoth had a bit more of the good stuff. Karel Vejmelka made 22 saves for the Mammoth, and Devon Levi stopped 20 of 23. By our Swing measure, Vincent Trocheck had the best night of anyone. The Mammoth improved to 6-2-0, and the Oilers fell to 5-1-1.
